title: China not opposed to Philippines defense partnerships, but...
summary: China, through its embassy in Manila, clarified yesterday that it is not against cooperation agreements between the Philippines and other countries.

blocks.text: However, such partnerships “must not undermine China’s sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, nor damage peace and stability in the South China Sea (SCS).”
MANILA, Philippines — China, through its embassy in Manila, clarified yesterday that it is not against cooperation agreements between the Philippines and other countries.

The statement issued through the embassy’s official social media pages apparently refers to defense cooperation agreements between the Philippines and its allied nations, most recently with Australia.

“China is committed to properly handling differences with the Philippines through dialogue and consultation and to safeguarding peace and stability in the South China Sea and the region,” the Chinese embassy said.
“China does not oppose normal cooperation between the Philippines and other countries,” the statement added.

The embassy said such partnerships should not affect “peace and stability in the South China Sea” including in the West Philippine Sea where there is a large presence of Chinese military, coast guard and maritime militia vessels.
China’s presence and behavior in waters within the 200-natutical mile exclusive economic zone of the Philippines has been described by the military as illegal, coercive, aggressive and deceptive.

Despite the 2016 Arbitral Award that invalidated China’s expansive maritime claims in the South China Sea, and which numerous countries including the United States recognize as final and binding, Chinese maritime assets including warships of the People’s Liberation Army Navy still patrol the WPS.
Meanwhile, Chinese Ministry of National Defense spokesman Senior Col. Chen Xi accused Japan of meddling in SCS issues allegedly for its own benefits.

“Under the disguise of academic research, Japan, in this report, whitewashes its moves to meddle in the South China Sea issue and stoke tensions across the Asia-Pacific, and smears China’s legitimate law-enforcement operations,” he said.

“This is yet another testament to the Japanese authorities’ ambition to build up its armed forces and break free from the ‘exclusively defense-oriented’ principle. The international community should stay highly vigilant against this,” Chen, in a statement also shared by the Chinese embassy, claimed.
Arguing that the SCS “is China’s inherent territory,” he said “Japan is not a party to the South China Sea issue, and is therefore in no position to make irresponsible remarks on it.”

“We require the Japanese side to stop fueling tensions over the South China Sea issue. Any attempt to challenge China’s sovereign rights and interests and undermine regional peace and stability will not succeed,” he added.
